                [32m'## Background\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"A documentation platform ingests HTML authored by many different tools. Before the HTML pipeline can be trusted, the platform team needs a repeatable **audit tool** that answers two questions about **Docling**'s HTML backend (the `docling` Python package and all of its dependencies are already installed in this environment):\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'1. **Structural fidelity** — how does the backend turn awkward real-world HTML (ordered lists with hostile `start` attributes, description lists, tables nested inside list items, deeply nested tables carrying images, line breaks, preformatted text, content that precedes the first heading, page footers) into a `DoclingDocument`?\n'[39m +
                [32m'2. **Resource-fetch policy** — when an HTML document references an external or local resource, which locations does the backend resolve, which does it refuse, and under which switches?\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'The audit must be reproducible and run **fully offline**: the tool must neither perform nor require any network I/O, and it must produce the same report on an air-gapped machine.                 [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Requirements\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m"* Convert every `*.html` fixture in a given directory with Docling's HTML backend, using the backend's **default** HTML backend options, and record structural facts about each resulting document: two markdown views (BODY content layer only, and BODY plus FURNITURE), table count, table shapes, table cell texts, and picture count.\n"[39m +
                [32m'* Run a fixed matrix of **resource-location resolutions** through the same resolution logic the HTML backend uses for locations found in a document, and record for each probe whether the location was resolved (and to what) or rejected (and with which error).\n'[39m +

                [32m"* Run a fixed set of URLs through the backend's remote-URL safety validation and record which are accepted and which are refused.\n"[39m +
                [32m'* Aggregate everything into a single JSON report.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* All facts in the report must be produced by actually exercising Docling in the current environment. The tool is a general audit tool: it will be pointed at different fixture directories and different local resource trees, and it must produce the correct report for whatever it is given.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Implementation Hints\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Project path: `/home/user/project`\n'[39m +

                [32m'    `python main.py --html-dir assets/html --local-root assets/local --report output/report.json`\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * All three flags are required. Paths may be relative to the working directory or absolute. Create parent directories of the report if they do not exist. On success, exit with code `0`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * If `--html-dir` or `--local-root` does not exist as a directory, write no report, print a diagnostic to stderr, and exit with code `2`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Two named base locations are used by the probe matrices below:\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * `LOCAL_BASE` — the **absolute** path of `<local_root>/page.html`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  * `REMOTE_BASE` — the literal string `https://cdn.example.com/docs/page.html`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Report format\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'The report is a single UTF-8 JSON object with exactly these top-level keys, in this order: `documents`, `resolution_probes`, `fetch_probes`, `url_safety_probes`, `summary`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'**`documents`** — one object per `*.html` file located directly in `<html_dir>` (non-recursive), ordered ascending by file name (Unicode code-point order). Each object has exactly these keys, in this order:\n'[39m +

                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'**`resolution_probes`** — one object per probe below, ordered ascending by `id`. Keys, in this order: `id` (string), `outcome` (string, `"resolved"` or `"rejected"`), `resolved` (the returned location string when resolved, otherwise `null`), `error_type` (the raised exception\'s class name when rejected, otherwise `null`), `error_message` (the raised exception rendered as a string when rejected, otherwise `null`).\n'[39m +

                    [32m'    """Reject URLs that resolve to a non-public IP address.\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m"    Guards against SSRF by requiring the URL's host to resolve to a globally\r\n"[39m +
                    [32m'    routable address. Private, loopback, link-local, reserved, multicast, and\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    unspecified addresses are refused.\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    Args:\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        url: The URL whose host is validated.\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    Raises:\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        ValueError: If the URL has no hostname, the hostname cannot be\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'            resolved, or it resolves to a restricted (non-global) IP address.\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    """\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    parsed = urlparse(url)\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    hostname = parsed.hostname\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    if not hostname:\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        raise ValueError("URL must contain a valid hostname")\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    try:\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        ip = ipaddress.ip_address(hostname)\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    except ValueError:\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        try:\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'            ip_str = socket.gethostbyname(hostname)\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'            ip = ipaddress.ip_address(ip_str)\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        except (socket.gaierror, socket.herror) as e:\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'            raise ValueError(f"Cannot resolve hostname: {hostname}") from e\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    if not (\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        ip.is_global\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        and not (\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'            ip.is_private\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'            or ip.is_loopback\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'            or ip.is_link_local\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'            or ip.is_reserved\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'            or ip.is_multicast\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'            or ip.is_unspecified\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        )\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    ):\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        raise ValueError(f"Access to restricted IP address not allowed: {ip}")\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\r\n'[39m +
                    [32m''[39m,

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m"Before using this tool, use the readFile tool to understand the file's contents and context\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'To make a file edit, provide the following:\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'   - Include AT LEAST 3-5 lines of context AFTER the change point\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'2. EXPECTED MATCHES: If you want to replace multiple instances:\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Use the expectedReplacements parameter with the exact number of occurrences you expect to replace\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - This will replace ALL occurrences of the searchContent with the replaceContent\n'[39m +
            [32m"   - If the actual number of matches doesn't equal expectedReplacements, the edit will fail\n"[39m +
            [32m'   - This is a safety feature to prevent unintended replacements\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. VERIFICATION: Before using this tool:\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Check how many instances of the target text exist in the file\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +

Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When users ask you to perform tasks, check if any of the available skills below can help complete the task more effectively. Skills provide specialized capabilities and domain knowledge.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m"This tool returns the skill's detailed instructions which you must then follow to complete the task. The instructions contain step-by-step guidance on how to perform the specific task or workflow.\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'How to invoke:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Use this tool with the skill name\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Example: `skill: "pdf-processing"` - invoke the pdf-processing skill\n'[39m +
            [32m"- The tool will return the skill's instructions\n"[39m +
            [32m'- Follow the returned instructions carefully to complete the task\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Important:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- NEVER just announce or mention a skill in your text response without actually calling this tool (except for general skill listing requests)\n'[39m +
            [32m'- This is a BLOCKING REQUIREMENT: invoke the relevant Skill tool BEFORE generating any other response about a specific skill or task\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Only use skills listed in "Available skills" below\n'[39m +

            [32m"- Use the directory containing the skill's source file as the base directory for resolving any resource files mentioned in the instructions\n"[39m +
            [32m'- Proactively explore the skill directory for optional resources that enhance task completion:\n'[39m +
            [32m'  * scripts/ - executable code that agents can run (Python, Bash, JavaScript, etc.)\n'[39m +

            [32m'When using the newTask tool, the agentType parameter is optional. Leave it empty (None) to launch a generic sub agent, or specify one of the available agent types below to select a specialized agent.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +
            [32m'Web browser automation agent for navigating websites, interacting with pages, and extracting information. Uses agent-browser CLI for browser control, including headless sessions and optional local Chrome auto-connect.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of questions this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "where is the authentication logic implemented"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "find all usages of the config parser"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +
            [32m"**IMPORTANT: Any request to modify Pochi's configuration must be handled by this agent.**\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Trigger examples:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- General info: "what can Pochi do?", "what agents/tools are available?", "how does Pochi work?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how should we refactor the database schema"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "design a solution for the memory leak issue"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### reviewer\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to perform code reviews and leave inline comments.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent can analyze code and create review comments on specific lines.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "review the code in src/auth"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "add review comments to this file"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "check this code and leave feedback"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Always include a reminder in your prompt to ensure the result will be submitted through the `attemptCompletion` tool.\n'[39m +
            [32m'If the task stops without submitting the result, it will return an error message.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When NOT to use the newTask tool:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you want to read a specific file path, use the readFile or globFiles tool instead of the newTask tool, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you are searching for a specific class definition like "class Foo", use the globFiles tool instead, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you are searching for code within a specific file or set of 2-3 files, use the readFile tool instead of the newTask tool, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Other tasks that are not related to the agent descriptions above\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. Launch multiple agents tools concurrently whenever possible to maximize performance; to do that, use a single message with multiple tool uses\n'[39m +
            [32m'2. When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report.
